model.title: Model
model.description: {brand} models. If yours is not listed, type it.

detalles.title: The appliance
detalles.description:
{product}

Prefilled from what we know about that model; correct it if your appliance differs.

abort.already_configured: That switch already has a trap attached.

init.title: Trap settings
init.description: Changing any of this does not reset the refill count.

conexion.name: Connection
conexion.description: Which socket it is plugged into. That is where the running hours come from, and running hours are what use the refill up.

aparato.name: The appliance
aparato.description: What the trap is. The model decides which refills it takes, and the mode how fast it burns them.

recarga.name: The refill
recarga.description: What is in the socket right now. Changing any of this does NOT restart the count — "New refill fitted" is what does that.

deteccion.name: Reading the mode from the power draw
deteccion.description: The trap's button is physical, so nothing tells Home Assistant it moved — but each mode draws a different, very steady amount of power, and that gives it away.

data.power_entity: Power meter (leave empty to find it automatically)
data.auto_mode: Change the mode by itself when the reading is unambiguous

aviso.name: Replacement warning
aviso.description: Hours per night is only used when a refill is rated in nights.

data.warn_percent: Warn when life left drops below

error.switch_in_use: That switch already powers “{other}”. Two traps counting the same socket would both be wrong, so this one has been left as it was.

replace_refill.name: New refill fitted
replace_refill.description: Registers that a new refill has been fitted and starts its count from zero. Only refill data: brand, model and mode belong to the appliance and are changed in the trap's options.

entity_id.name: Trap
entity_id.description: Any entity of the trap, normally its “Life left” sensor.

refill.name: Refill
refill.description: Which refill was fitted. Leave empty to keep the current one.

target.name: What it is for
target.description: The same appliance takes refills for different insects.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: The number printed on the box.

duration_unit.name: Duration unit
duration_unit.description: Whether that number is nights or plain running hours.

reset.name: Start the count from zero
reset.description: On by default. Turn it off to correct a detail without losing the hours already counted.

fitted_at.name: Fitted at
fitted_at.description: When it actually went in. Empty means now. Only the date moves; the count still starts at zero.

warn_percent.name: Warn below
warn_percent.description: Life left at which the trap starts asking for a new refill.

remove_refill.name: Refill taken out
remove_refill.description: Records that the socket is empty. The trap stops reporting a percentage and says it has no refill, which is what it should say when there is nothing left in it to evaporate.

entity_id.name: Trap
entity_id.description: Any entity of the trap, normally its “Life left” sensor.

recalibrate.name: Relearn the power reference
recalibrate.description: Forgets the draw this trap learned as its baseline and learns it again from whatever mode it is set to now. Use it when the reference was learned while the mode was wrong, which poisons every later judgement.

entity_id.name: Trap
entity_id.description: Any entity of the trap, normally its “Life left” sensor.

v1_storage.title: {name}: confirm which refill is fitted
v1_storage.description:
This trap was counting with an older format that had no way to say whether a refill was actually fitted, so its {hours} h tally could not be carried over. It now reports “no refill” rather than a comfortable 100 %.

Press “New refill fitted” once and this goes away.
